source_title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he left Brazil because he is the victim of 'persecution'
source_excerpt: Brasília Former conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said Friday (October 30, 2026) that he fled Brazil to the United States because he was a victim of "persecution" in his country. Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's (October 25) election runoff to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, secretly left Brazil on Tuesday (October 27) and arrived in Florida aboard a private jet on Wednesday (October 28) after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador. Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Florida after election defeat storyline 1 Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to U.S. Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to U.S. “I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny,” Flavio Bolsonaro said; U.S. President Donald Trump said he “won’t get involved” in Mr. Bolsonaro’s claim Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to U.S. storyline 1 "The persecution began even sooner than I imagined," the senator said during an Instagram livestream in which he discussed his decision to flee after his Brazilian passports were cancelled as part of a money laundering investigation. In the video, he recounted how police informed him on Monday that his passports were being revoked as he left a visit to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest. "I told him: 'Dad, I know... Now I know what I have to do,'" he recounted. Bolsonaro's getaway plane paid for from U.S. bank: Airline Bolsonaro's getaway plane paid for from U.S. bank: Airline Following the vote, the 45-year-old snuck out of Brazil via Argentina and Ecuador in a cloak-and-dagger operation, after being ordered to surrender his passports due to several ongoing investigations against him Bolsonaro's getaway plane paid for from U.S. bank: Airline storyline 1 Although he gave no details of how he left the country, he said he and his wife made the decision "without anyone knowing" and urged people not to "point the finger at anyone." U.S. President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei are under pressure to explain the involvement of the United States and Argentina in the senator's escape. "I didn't leave Brazil; I left for Brazil," Flavio Bolsonaro said, alleging that Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had made false accusations against him. He also suggested there had been irregularities in the runoff, comparing them to "handball goals" that were not disallowed by VAR, without detailing what those irregularities might have been. He also predicted that the economy would "go bust" under Lula and said he was willing to run for president again: "I'm not talking about 2030, I'm talking about before then."
